name: External iliac vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Femoral vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Great (long) saphenous vein
notes: Longest vein in the body; ascends from the medial malleolus to the saphenofemoral junction; common CABG graft and varicose-vein site.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Popliteal vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Small (short) saphenous vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior tibial veins (venae comitantes)
supplies_or_drains: deep anterior compartment of leg, accompanying anterior tibial artery territory
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior tibial veins (venae comitantes)
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Fibular veins (venae comitantes)
supplies_or_drains: deep lateral compartment of leg, accompanying fibular artery territory
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Dorsal venous arch of the foot
notes: Superficial arch; origin of the great and small saphenous veins.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Perforating veins (of the leg)
notes: Connect the superficial (saphenous) and deep venous systems through the deep fascia; contain one-way valves directing flow superficial-to-deep -- valve failure here is a major cause of venous ulceration.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.6; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Common femoral vein
notes: The segment between the saphenofemoral junction and the inguinal ligament. Lies MEDIAL to the femoral artery at the groin, which is the basis of femoral venous puncture one finger's breadth medial to the arterial pulse.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep femoral (profunda femoris) vein
notes: Provides the main collateral route when the femoral vein is occluded, which is why isolated femoral vein thrombosis can be clinically quiet.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior accessory saphenous vein
notes: Runs parallel and lateral to the great saphenous vein, joining it near the saphenofemoral junction. A common source of recurrent varicose veins after an otherwise adequate great saphenous ablation, because it is easily missed on duplex.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior accessory saphenous vein
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior arch vein (vein of Leonardo)
supplies_or_drains: medial calf, via the medial calf (Cockett) perforators
notes: Runs behind the great saphenous vein up the medial calf and receives the Cockett perforators. Incompetence of those perforators is classically associated with the medial gaiter ulcer of chronic venous insufficiency.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Soleal venous sinuses
notes: Large valveless sinusoids inside soleus, emptied by the calf muscle pump. The commonest site of origin for calf deep vein thrombosis, because stasis there is greatest during immobility -- the anatomical reason early mobilisation and calf compression work as prophylaxis.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Gastrocnemius (sural) veins
supplies_or_drains: medial and lateral heads of gastrocnemius
notes: Drain directly into the popliteal vein. Isolated gastrocnemius vein thrombosis is a recognised duplex finding whose management is debated, unlike thrombosis of the popliteal vein itself.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial plantar veins
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral plantar veins
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Plantar venous plexus
notes: Compressed at each heel strike, acting as the first stage of the venous pump before the calf muscles take over. This is the physiological basis of intermittent pneumatic foot compression.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Saphenopopliteal junction perforator
supplies_or_drains: connection from the small saphenous vein to the popliteal vein
notes: One of the most variable junctions in the body: its level relative to the knee crease, and whether it exists at all, differ enough that duplex marking before small saphenous surgery is standard.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
